name: Freshman Seminar for Computing
summary: Introduces new Bellini College students to degree choices, academic requirements and support resources.
rationale: The entire description is first-year orientation and academic navigation; it does not establish programming or other computing subject content.

name: Programming Concepts
summary: Introduces programming concepts and design methods through a contemporary programming language.
rationale: The description expressly centers programming and software design.

name: Program Design
summary: Develops program design and construction using C in a networked environment.
rationale: Program construction is the central subject; a networked setting does not make this a networking-infrastructure course.

name: Data Structures
summary: Studies and implements data structures for clear, efficient programs, including functional-programming concepts.
rationale: The description centers data structures, representations and programming.

name: Composition I
summary: Introduces rhetorical analysis, audience-aware writing, composition processes and language conventions.
rationale: Rhetoric and written communication are the explicit subjects.

name: Composition II
summary: Practices effective reading, writing and public speaking.
rationale: The description centers human communication.

name: Calculus I
summary: Studies single-variable limits, derivatives and integrals, with optimization and other applications.
rationale: Calculus concepts and mathematical problem solving are explicit.

name: Calculus II
summary: Develops integration, series and elementary transcendental functions for mathematical problem solving.
rationale: The description centers calculus and mathematical methods.

name: General Physics I - Calculus Based
summary: Introduces calculus-based mechanics, fluids, oscillations and waves for science and engineering students.
rationale: Physics is substantive domain knowledge; using calculus does not make the course mathematical theory or computing foundations.

name: General Physics I Laboratory
summary: Provides the first laboratory in the two-semester general-physics sequence for physics and engineering students.
rationale: Experimental physics is the stated domain practice; the whole sequence topic list is not a claim that this laboratory alone covers every listed topic.

name: Computer Organization
summary: Introduces digital hardware, processor organization, memory and I/O, with computer arithmetic and assembly programming.
rationale: Computer architecture and hardware organization dominate the description.

name: Introduction to Discrete Structures
summary: Introduces sets, propositional logic and finite algebraic structures with computing applications.
rationale: The actual description centers mathematical structures and logic, rather than implementing data structures or algorithms.

name: Analysis of Algorithms
summary: Studies design principles and analytical techniques for commonly used computer algorithms.
rationale: Algorithm design and analysis are explicit computing foundations.

name: Probability and Statistics with Calculus
summary: Introduces probability and statistical analysis, with critical data interpretation and problem solving.
rationale: Probability and statistical methods are the named subject, independent of the engineering prefix.

name: Introduction to Linear Systems
summary: Studies matrix algebra, differential equations and finite differences.
rationale: The description is mathematical methods; the title does not establish computing systems.

name: Introduction to Psychological Science
summary: Introduces scientific study of human behavior and mental processes through historical and current psychological perspectives.
rationale: The description centers human behavior and cognition; it does not state an AI methods curriculum.

name: Natural Language Processing
summary: Introduces computational natural-language processing through linguistic phenomena, formal methods and applications.
rationale: Natural-language processing is an explicitly described AI-focused subfield.

name: Introductory Statistics I
summary: Applies descriptive and inferential statistics to data interpretation and contextual problems.
rationale: Statistical methods are explicit; application across disciplines does not change the primary subject.

name: American National Government
summary: Studies U.S. constitutional government, its historical foundations, institutions, policies and citizen participation.
rationale: Political institutions and civic participation are the primary subject.

name: American History I
summary: Examines U.S. history before European contact through Reconstruction, including constitutional development, slavery and the Civil War.
rationale: The description explicitly studies social and political history.

name: American History II
summary: Traces U.S. history after Reconstruction through the contemporary era, including industrialization, war, constitutional change and civil rights.
rationale: The description explicitly studies social and political history.
